name: consent
whenToEnable: Record consent the way a regulator asks to see it, in your own D1. Purposes are declared and versioned: email declares marketing and tracking, and you add your own with the data classes each covers, whether it is explicit, and the weakest method a grant may be given by — a click, a typed name, a drawn signature, or an e-signature provider's completed envelope. Bump a notice version and every older grant needs renewing. Every grant and withdrawal is an append-only row the database itself refuses to change, and an audit event, so the tamper-evident trail covers it. A signed grant keeps the exact document by its hash, the signature, how identity was verified, an expiry and a representative, with the names encrypted at rest. Visitors consent against an anonymous device id held only once they choose, merged into their account at sign-in. hasConsent is the one question every capability asks, and email's tracking and marketing mail follow it. Writes wear auth's same-origin gate, so add auth too.
scaffold: Add a `consent()` block to pithy.config.ts. Email's purposes, `email.marketing` and `email.tracking`, are composed for you.

Declare your own purposes under your own domain in `consent({ purposes })`: an id, a summary written for the person, a notice version, the data classes it covers, whether it is explicit, the minimum method, and whether a withdrawal must be written.
Run `pithy migrate` to create pithy_consent_records, pithy_consent_documents and pithy_consent_merges.
Run `pithy secrets provision`: the typed and representative names are encrypted fields, so the Worker needs PITHY_FIELD_KEYS.
Bind the R2 bucket CONSENT_EVIDENCE if you take drawn signatures or a provider's certificates. `pithy provision` creates it.
Pass `consentSubject` when you enqueue marketing mail, so email can ask whose consent it is sent under.
Run `pithy ui add react --consent` for the settings screen a person reads and withdraws their consents on.

configOptions.describe: Your own purposes, beside the ones composed capabilities declare. Each under your own domain — `clinic.records` — with a summary, a notice version, its data classes, whether it is explicit, its minimum method and whether a withdrawal must be written.
How many days a visitor's consent counts while it has not been merged into an account. The device-id cookie lives as long.
Where the consent routes mount: the purposes, the person's own record, grants, withdrawals and the control-plane reads.
